summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified. TypeScript compiles clean (tsc --noEmit, zero errors). New test file tests/schema/common.test.ts passes all 4 tests. Full regression suite: 3,868 tests across 135 files — all pass. Edge-case analysis confirmed: SLUG_REGEX correctly rejects empty strings, leading hyphens/underscores, spaces, slashes, dots, path traversal sequences, and implicitly rejects Unicode via explicit ASCII character class. common.ts has zero imports eliminating any circular import risk. Backward-compat re-export from knowledge.ts preserves identical regex source and flags.

comments.note: SLUG_REGEX has no maximum-length constraint. Very long slugs are accepted syntactically. Not a defect for current use cases (storage paths), but worth noting for future hardening.

No existing imports in gui/api-knowledge.ts or src/tools/knowledge.ts were migrated to common.ts — both still import from knowledge.js. This is correct per the WP scope, and the backward-compat re-export keeps them functional. Future work could migrate them for clarity.

summary: Code review PASS. The implementation is architecturally sound and correctly scoped.

common.ts is a clean zero-import module — the right home for a cross-domain constant. The file-level JSDoc clearly explains the rationale (avoid coupling unrelated schema files), which is exactly the guidance future contributors need.

The aliased import pattern in knowledge.ts (`import { SLUG_REGEX as _SLUG_REGEX }`) is idiomatic TypeScript for disambiguation when re-exporting under the same name. The @deprecated tag gives forward direction without breaking anything.
The three updated importers (store-config.ts, repository-registry.ts, gui/api-repos.ts) each have only the import line changed — no behavioral drift. Confirmed by inspection.

Tests in common.test.ts are well-structured: export-presence test, backward-compat test comparing .source and .flags, valid-slug batch test with representative cases, and invalid-slug batch test including path-traversal sequences. Coverage is appropriate for a regex utility.

Remaining consumers (knowledge-store.ts, tools/knowledge.ts) still import from knowledge.ts via the deprecated re-export — correct per WP scope. The re-export is a clean bridge; those consumers can be migrated as follow-on work.

comments.note: common.ts zero-import design is excellent defensive practice — eliminates circular-import risk permanently for this constant, regardless of how many future consumers are added.

[documentation-forward] Two consumers remain on the deprecated knowledge.ts re-export: src/storage/knowledge-store.ts and src/tools/knowledge.ts. Document these as known migration candidates in api-surface.md or file-tree.md notes — the @deprecated tag in knowledge.ts is sufficient for IDE tooling but a manifest-level note would make the migration surface visible in code-review checklists.

The backward-compat test in common.test.ts compares .source and .flags rather than referential identity (===). Both are correct; the property comparison is arguably more explicit about what backward-compat means (same pattern and flags), but callers depending on referential identity could be validated with a single expect(SLUG_REGEX_FROM_KNOWLEDGE).toBe(SLUG_REGEX) assertion as a complement — not blocking, purely additive.
